summary: Solo hiker called for help near the summit of 14,075-ft Mount Columbia around 7:25 p.m., more than two hours after sunset; the subject reported being uninjured but extremely cold and unable to feel their feet, and was unprepared to spend the night on the mountain. CCSAR-N deployed a ground team with warming equipment and Flight for Life inserted a team member with warming supplies, but high winds ruled out a helicopter extraction; the inserted rescuer made contact and warmed the hiker, who was then walked out — mission complete 5:30 a.m. November 3.
location: near the summit of Mt. Columbia (14,075 ft)
responding_agency: Chaffee County Search and Rescue North; Flight for Life
notes: Recorded at call date 2024-11-02 (Saturday, weekday-verified); mission completed 05:30 on 2024-11-03. Solo hiker identity not published. Cold-exposure/incipient frostbite but reported uninjured — classified rescued-uninjured. Surfaced via Mountain Mail rotation-chunk searches of Chaffee-area SAR stories (local MM coverage did not surface; both URLs opened this run).
